## Other work and media image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sakshi_Tanwar&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other work and media image")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b9/Sakshi_Tanwar_at_the_success_party_of_%E2%80%98Dangal%E2%80%99.jpg/250px-Sakshi_Tanwar_at_the_success_party_of_%E2%80%98Dangal%E2%80%99.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sakshi_Tanwar_at_the_success_party_of_%E2%80%98Dangal%E2%80%99.jpg)

Tanwar at _[Dangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangal\_(2016\_film) "Dangal (2016 film)")_'s success party in 2017

With her performances in _Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii_, _Kutumb_, _Devi_ and _Bade Achhe Lagte Hain_, Tanwar established herself among the leading and highest-paid actresses of Hindi television.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-highest-paidd-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-highest-paid-2)_[Rediff.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff.com "Rediff.com")_ placed her first in its "Top TV stars of 2006" and tenth in its "Top 10 television actresses" list.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-46) Supriya Sharma of _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ termed her the "nation's most-loved telly star".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-47) Tanwar is termed as one of the hottest television actress by Rediff.com.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-48) In 2022, _[Forbes India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes\_India "Forbes India")_ included her in its first ever "Showstoppers – India's Top 50 Outperformers" list.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-49)

In 2012, Tanwar appeared in _[Forbes India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes\_India "Forbes India")_'s[Celebrity 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_Celebrity_100 "Forbes Celebrity 100") list, ranking 93rd with an estimated annual income of ₹34.5 million (US$360,000).[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-50) Her on-screen pairing with [Ram Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram_Kapoor "Ram Kapoor") was voted as "Television's most popular onscreen couple", in an _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ survey.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-51) In April 2013, in a survey conducted by _Ormax Media_, Tanwar featured in the "Top 5 most trustworthy celebrities" list.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-dnaindia-8) In a 2014 poll conducted by _[Shaadi.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaadi.com "Shaadi.com")_, Tanwar and Kapoor were voted the _Favourite TV Couple_ by 42.3% Indians.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-Jan-IBNLive-52) Tanwar is also a celebrity endorser for brands and products such as [Vim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vim_(cleaning_product) "Vim (cleaning product)"), [Harpic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harpic "Harpic"), [Tanishq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanishq "Tanishq"), [Kellogg's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellogg's "Kellogg's") and [Big Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Bazaar "Big Bazaar"). _[Economic Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Economic\_Times "The Economic Times")_ termed her the "second-most visible celebrity on television", in 2016.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakshi_Tanwar#cite_note-53)

**Sriti Jha** (pronounced[[ˈsɾɪt̪i d͡ʒʱaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born 26 February 1986) is an Indian actress who primarily works in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") television. Noted for her versatility in a range of genres from romantic comedies to crime dramas, she is a recipient of several accolades including two [ITA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Television_Academy_Awards "Indian Television Academy Awards"), three [Indian Telly Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Telly_Awards "Indian Telly Awards") and two [Gold Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Awards "Gold Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-HindustanT-1)

Jha made her acting debut in 2007 with the [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama"), _[Dhoom Machaao Dhoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhoom\_Machaao\_Dhoom "Dhoom Machaao Dhoom")_, playing Malini Sharma. Jha then established herself as a [leading actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leading_actress "Leading actress") with her portrayal of Sudha "Devika" Sharma Vashisht in _[Jyoti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyoti\_(TV\_series) "Jyoti (TV series)")_, Sandhya Savratkar Pradhan in _[Rakt Sambandh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakt\_Sambandh "Rakt Sambandh")_ and Jhanvi Dobriyal / Sia Pratapsingh in _[Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se\_Di\_Dua...\_Saubhagyavati\_Bhava%3F "Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?")_. Jha earned wider recognition with her portrayal of Pragya Arora Mehra in _[Kumkum Bhagya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumkum\_Bhagya "Kumkum Bhagya")_. In 2022, she participated in _[Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear\_Factor:\_Khatron\_Ke\_Khiladi\_12 "Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12")_, where she finished at 10th place and became the 3rd runner-up in _[Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalak\_Dikhhla\_Jaa\_(season\_10) "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa (season 10)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-HindustanT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-Times-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jha was born on 26 February 1986 in [Begusarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begusarai "Begusarai"), [Bihar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar "Bihar").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-Times_of_India_Sriti_Jha_turns_31-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-4) She went to live with her family in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), where they stayed for 10 years, then moved to [Kathmandu, Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathmandu,_Nepal "Kathmandu, Nepal"). They then moved to [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), where she continued her studies at Laxman Public School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-factstoi-5) She completed her Bachelor of Arts degree in English at [Sri Venkateswara College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Venkateswara_College "Sri Venkateswara College"), [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"). She has an elder sister, Meenakshi and a younger brother, Shashank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Debut and early breakthrough (2007-2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Debut and early breakthrough (2007-2013)")]

Jha made her acting debut in 2007 playing Malini Sharma in [Disney India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel_(Indian_TV_channel) "Disney Channel (Indian TV channel)")'s teen drama _[Dhoom Machaao Dhoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhoom\_Machaao\_Dhoom "Dhoom Machaao Dhoom")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-toi1-8) In 2008, she played Sunaina Kotak opposite [Saurabh Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurabh_Pandey "Saurabh Pandey") in _[Jiya Jale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiya\_Jale "Jiya Jale")_ and also participated in the friend-based reality show _[Kaho Na Yaar Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaho\_Na\_Yaar\_Hai "Kaho Na Yaar Hai")_. Jha played Suhani, a royal princess in _[Shaurya Aur Suhani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaurya\_Aur\_Suhani "Shaurya Aur Suhani")_, opposite Saurabh Pandey, in 2009.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-9)

Jha's first major role was in _[Jyoti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyoti\_(TV\_series) "Jyoti (TV series)")_, where she played Sudha Sharma, a split personality patient opposite Alok Narula, from 2009 to 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-10) In 2010, Jha played a visually impaired girl, Sandhya Savratkar Pradhan opposite [Naman Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naman_Shaw "Naman Shaw") and [Dhruv Bhandari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhruv_Bhandari "Dhruv Bhandari") in _[Rakt Sambandh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakt\_Sambandh "Rakt Sambandh")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-11) Critic from _[The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Indian\_Express "The Indian Express")_ noted, "Sriti is well cast as she brings a certain vulnerability and quiet strength to her character." In that year, she appeared as a contestant on _[Nachle Ve with Saroj Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nachle\_Ve\_with\_Saroj\_Khan "Nachle Ve with Saroj Khan")_ and _[Meethi Choori No 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meethi\_Choori\_No\_1 "Meethi Choori No 1")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-12)

From 2011 to 2013, Jha portrayed Jhanvi Sharma Dobriyal / Sia Sharma Pratapsingh, a victim of domestic violence in _[Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se\_Di\_Dua...\_Saubhagyavati\_Bhava%3F "Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?")_, opposite [Harshad Chopda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshad_Chopda "Harshad Chopda") and [Karanvir Bohra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karanvir_Bohra "Karanvir Bohra"). The show proved to be her breakthrough and earned her recognition.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-14) In 2013, Jha also played Ganga Singh opposite [Shashank Vyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashank_Vyas "Shashank Vyas") in _[Balika Vadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balika\_Vadhu "Balika Vadhu")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-15)

From 2014 to 2021, Jha portrayed Pragya Arora Mehra in [Ekta Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ekta_Kapoor "Ekta Kapoor")'s _[Kumkum Bhagya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumkum\_Bhagya "Kumkum Bhagya")_ opposite Shabir Ahluwalia.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-17) The series earned her critical acclaim, success and established her among the leading actresses of Indian television.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-18) Her portrayal of Pragya earned her various accolades including [ITA Award for Best Actress - Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Drama_-_Jury "ITA Award for Best Actress in a Drama - Jury") and [Indian Telly Award for Best Actress in a Lead Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Telly_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Lead_Role "Indian Telly Award for Best Actress in a Lead Role").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-19)

Alongside her role in _Kumkum Bhagya_, Jha acted as the narrator for _[Naagin 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naagin\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Naagin (2015 TV series)")_ in 2016.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-20) She also played Deepa in the 2020 short film _U-Turn_ and in 2021, she played Sakshi Deewan in the podcast series _Darmiyaan_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-21)

In 2022, Jha first participated in _[Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear\_Factor:\_Khatron\_Ke\_Khiladi\_12 "Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12")_ and ended up finishing at the 10th place.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-23) In the same year, she participated in _[Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalak\_Dikhhla\_Jaa\_(season\_10) "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa (season 10)")_, as a wildcard entry and finished as the 3rd runner-up.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-24)

### Recent work (2023-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Recent work (2023-present)")]

In 2023, Jha played Jaya, an actress in [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar")'s _[Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky\_Aur\_Rani\_Kii\_Prem\_Kahaani "Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-25) In the same year, she appeared as the ghost of Jhanvi / Sia in _[Saubhagyavati Bhava: * Niyam Aur Shartein Laagu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saubhagyavati\_Bhava:\_*\_Niyam\_Aur\_Shartein\_Laagu "Saubhagyavati Bhava: * Niyam Aur Shartein Laagu")_, a sequel to her 2011 series. She played a working wife in the short film _Chawal_, alongside Nihal Parashar, in the same year.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-26)

From November 2023 to May 2025, Jha is seen playing Amruta Bhavani Chitnis, a banker opposite [Arjit Taneja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjit_Taneja "Arjit Taneja") in _Kaise Mujhe Tum Mil Gaye_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-28)

## Other work and public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other work and public image")]

Jha at an event in 2018

Jha's acting performances in the series - _Jyoti_, _Rakt Sambandh_, _Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?_ and _Kumkum Bhagya_, established her among the leading and highest-paid actresses of the Hindi television.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-32) Jha is widely known for her style and fashion sense.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-33)

For her performance as Pragya in _Kumkum Bhagya_, _[The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Indian\_Express "The Indian Express")_ placed her at fifth position in its "Top 10 television actresses" list of 2017.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-34)_[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ noted Jha's different portrayals and appearances mainly in female-led shows and roles.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-35) Jha and Shabir Ahluwalia's pair was named among the "Best jodis of television" in 2014.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-37) Jha is a celebrity endorser for brands including, [Accessorize India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_Accessorize "Monsoon Accessorize"), Belleza, and Kalki Fashion and [Nupur Henna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godrej_Group "Godrej Group").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-38) In 2020, Jha became a part of a fundraiser for people affected by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). In 2023, Jha along with the cast of _Kaise Mujhe Tum Mil Gaye_ and _Kumkum Bhagya_, celebrated [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas "Christmas") with SNEHA foundation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-40)

In addition to her acting career, Jha also recite poems and does live shows. In January 2021, Jha recited a poem, "Confessions Of An Asexual Romantic", during the 2020 Kommune India Spoken Fest, in which she spoke about how the life of an asexual might be and how there is a lack of freedom in India when it comes to talking about one's sexuality.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-41) In an interview, she clarified she is not an asexual and that the poem isn't about her.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-42) She also recited two more poems regarding people with different sexual preferences and the problems they face such as "Choodiyaan" which talks about a gay male,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-43) and "Chaabi Gum Gai Hai", based on a lesbian female.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-:022-44) In "It's Pehla Pyaar Every Time", she talks about how every time we fall in love, it feels as if it's the first time.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-45)

Her other works, such as "To Like? Or To Love?" differentiate between loving and liking and how liking is free of boundaries while love is limiting.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-46) Jha's first open letter "A Letter To Myself" is about what she wants to tell her 15-year-old self in the past and that we should never compromise under any circumstance.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-47) In this collaboration with ITC Vivel, Jha inspires women to uncondition, challenge stereotypes and go forth to fulfill their dreams with confidence and say out loud, "Ab Samjhauta Nahin". She also presented a poem "Cheesy Stupid Ishq", as a narrator a day before the Valentines Day in 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-48)

**Sriti Jha** (pronounced[[ˈsɾɪt̪i d͡ʒʱaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born 26 February 1986) is an Indian actress who primarily works in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") television. Noted for her versatility in a range of genres from romantic comedies to crime dramas, she is a recipient of several accolades including two [ITA Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Television_Academy_Awards "Indian Television Academy Awards"), three [Indian Telly Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Telly_Awards "Indian Telly Awards") and two [Gold Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_Awards "Gold Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-HindustanT-1)

Jha made her acting debut in 2007 with the [teen drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_drama "Teen drama"), _[Dhoom Machaao Dhoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhoom\_Machaao\_Dhoom "Dhoom Machaao Dhoom")_, playing Malini Sharma. Jha then established herself as a [leading actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leading_actress "Leading actress") with her portrayal of Sudha "Devika" Sharma Vashisht in _[Jyoti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyoti\_(TV\_series) "Jyoti (TV series)")_, Sandhya Savratkar Pradhan in _[Rakt Sambandh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakt\_Sambandh "Rakt Sambandh")_ and Jhanvi Dobriyal / Sia Pratapsingh in _[Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se\_Di\_Dua...\_Saubhagyavati\_Bhava%3F "Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?")_. Jha earned wider recognition with her portrayal of Pragya Arora Mehra in _[Kumkum Bhagya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumkum\_Bhagya "Kumkum Bhagya")_. In 2022, she participated in _[Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear\_Factor:\_Khatron\_Ke\_Khiladi\_12 "Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12")_, where she finished at 10th place and became the 3rd runner-up in _[Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalak\_Dikhhla\_Jaa\_(season\_10) "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa (season 10)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-HindustanT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-Times-2)

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Jha was born on 26 February 1986 in [Begusarai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Begusarai "Begusarai"), [Bihar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bihar "Bihar").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-Times_of_India_Sriti_Jha_turns_31-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-4) She went to live with her family in [Kolkata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolkata "Kolkata"), where they stayed for 10 years, then moved to [Kathmandu, Nepal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathmandu,_Nepal "Kathmandu, Nepal"). They then moved to [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"), where she continued her studies at Laxman Public School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-factstoi-5) She completed her Bachelor of Arts degree in English at [Sri Venkateswara College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Venkateswara_College "Sri Venkateswara College"), [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi"). She has an elder sister, Meenakshi and a younger brother, Shashank.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-7)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Debut and early breakthrough (2007-2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Debut and early breakthrough (2007-2013)")]

Jha made her acting debut in 2007 playing Malini Sharma in [Disney India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney_Channel_(Indian_TV_channel) "Disney Channel (Indian TV channel)")'s teen drama _[Dhoom Machaao Dhoom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhoom\_Machaao\_Dhoom "Dhoom Machaao Dhoom")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-toi1-8) In 2008, she played Sunaina Kotak opposite [Saurabh Pandey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saurabh_Pandey "Saurabh Pandey") in _[Jiya Jale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiya\_Jale "Jiya Jale")_ and also participated in the friend-based reality show _[Kaho Na Yaar Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaho\_Na\_Yaar\_Hai "Kaho Na Yaar Hai")_. Jha played Suhani, a royal princess in _[Shaurya Aur Suhani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaurya\_Aur\_Suhani "Shaurya Aur Suhani")_, opposite Saurabh Pandey, in 2009.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-9)

Jha's first major role was in _[Jyoti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jyoti\_(TV\_series) "Jyoti (TV series)")_, where she played Sudha Sharma, a split personality patient opposite Alok Narula, from 2009 to 2010.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-10) In 2010, Jha played a visually impaired girl, Sandhya Savratkar Pradhan opposite [Naman Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naman_Shaw "Naman Shaw") and [Dhruv Bhandari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhruv_Bhandari "Dhruv Bhandari") in _[Rakt Sambandh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakt\_Sambandh "Rakt Sambandh")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-11) Critic from _[The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Indian\_Express "The Indian Express")_ noted, "Sriti is well cast as she brings a certain vulnerability and quiet strength to her character." In that year, she appeared as a contestant on _[Nachle Ve with Saroj Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nachle\_Ve\_with\_Saroj\_Khan "Nachle Ve with Saroj Khan")_ and _[Meethi Choori No 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meethi\_Choori\_No\_1 "Meethi Choori No 1")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-12)

From 2011 to 2013, Jha portrayed Jhanvi Sharma Dobriyal / Sia Sharma Pratapsingh, a victim of domestic violence in _[Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Se\_Di\_Dua...\_Saubhagyavati\_Bhava%3F "Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?")_, opposite [Harshad Chopda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshad_Chopda "Harshad Chopda") and [Karanvir Bohra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karanvir_Bohra "Karanvir Bohra"). The show proved to be her breakthrough and earned her recognition.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-14) In 2013, Jha also played Ganga Singh opposite [Shashank Vyas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashank_Vyas "Shashank Vyas") in _[Balika Vadhu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balika\_Vadhu "Balika Vadhu")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-15)

### Established actress (2014-2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Established actress (2014-2022)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Sriti_Jha_Snapshot.png/250px-Sriti_Jha_Snapshot.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sriti_Jha_Snapshot.png)

Jha in a scene of _[Kumkum Bhagya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumkum\_Bhagya "Kumkum Bhagya")_

From 2014 to 2021, Jha portrayed Pragya Arora Mehra in [Ekta Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ekta_Kapoor "Ekta Kapoor")'s _[Kumkum Bhagya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumkum\_Bhagya "Kumkum Bhagya")_ opposite Shabir Ahluwalia.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-17) The series earned her critical acclaim, success and established her among the leading actresses of Indian television.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-18) Her portrayal of Pragya earned her various accolades including [ITA Award for Best Actress - Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Drama_-_Jury "ITA Award for Best Actress in a Drama - Jury") and [Indian Telly Award for Best Actress in a Lead Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Telly_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Lead_Role "Indian Telly Award for Best Actress in a Lead Role").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-19)

Alongside her role in _Kumkum Bhagya_, Jha acted as the narrator for _[Naagin 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naagin\_(2015\_TV\_series) "Naagin (2015 TV series)")_ in 2016.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-20) She also played Deepa in the 2020 short film _U-Turn_ and in 2021, she played Sakshi Deewan in the podcast series _Darmiyaan_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-21)

In 2022, Jha first participated in _[Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fear\_Factor:\_Khatron\_Ke\_Khiladi\_12 "Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 12")_ and ended up finishing at the 10th place.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-23) In the same year, she participated in _[Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhalak\_Dikhhla\_Jaa\_(season\_10) "Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa (season 10)")_, as a wildcard entry and finished as the 3rd runner-up.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-24)

### Recent work (2023-present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Recent work (2023-present)")]

In 2023, Jha played Jaya, an actress in [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar")'s _[Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky\_Aur\_Rani\_Kii\_Prem\_Kahaani "Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani")_.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-25) In the same year, she appeared as the ghost of Jhanvi / Sia in _[Saubhagyavati Bhava: * Niyam Aur Shartein Laagu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saubhagyavati\_Bhava:\_*\_Niyam\_Aur\_Shartein\_Laagu "Saubhagyavati Bhava: * Niyam Aur Shartein Laagu")_, a sequel to her 2011 series. She played a working wife in the short film _Chawal_, alongside Nihal Parashar, in the same year.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-26)

From November 2023 to May 2025, Jha is seen playing Amruta Bhavani Chitnis, a banker opposite [Arjit Taneja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjit_Taneja "Arjit Taneja") in _Kaise Mujhe Tum Mil Gaye_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-28)

## Other work and public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sriti_Jha&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Other work and public image")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4c/Sriti_Jha_zt_Zee-Rishtey-Awards_2018_%28cropped_1%29.jpg/250px-Sriti_Jha_zt_Zee-Rishtey-Awards_2018_%28cropped_1%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sriti_Jha_zt_Zee-Rishtey-Awards_2018_(cropped_1).jpg)

Jha at an event in 2018

Jha's acting performances in the series - _Jyoti_, _Rakt Sambandh_, _Dil Se Di Dua... Saubhagyavati Bhava?_ and _Kumkum Bhagya_, established her among the leading and highest-paid actresses of the Hindi television.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-32) Jha is widely known for her style and fashion sense.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-33)

For her performance as Pragya in _Kumkum Bhagya_, _[The Indian Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Indian\_Express "The Indian Express")_ placed her at fifth position in its "Top 10 television actresses" list of 2017.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-34)_[The Times of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Times\_of\_India "The Times of India")_ noted Jha's different portrayals and appearances mainly in female-led shows and roles.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-35) Jha and Shabir Ahluwalia's pair was named among the "Best jodis of television" in 2014.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-37) Jha is a celebrity endorser for brands including, [Accessorize India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon_Accessorize "Monsoon Accessorize"), Belleza, and Kalki Fashion and [Nupur Henna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godrej_Group "Godrej Group").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-38) In 2020, Jha became a part of a fundraiser for people affected by the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). In 2023, Jha along with the cast of _Kaise Mujhe Tum Mil Gaye_ and _Kumkum Bhagya_, celebrated [Christmas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas "Christmas") with SNEHA foundation.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-40)

In addition to her acting career, Jha also recite poems and does live shows. In January 2021, Jha recited a poem, "Confessions Of An Asexual Romantic", during the 2020 Kommune India Spoken Fest, in which she spoke about how the life of an asexual might be and how there is a lack of freedom in India when it comes to talking about one's sexuality.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-41) In an interview, she clarified she is not an asexual and that the poem isn't about her.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-42) She also recited two more poems regarding people with different sexual preferences and the problems they face such as "Choodiyaan" which talks about a gay male,[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-43) and "Chaabi Gum Gai Hai", based on a lesbian female.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-:022-44) In "It's Pehla Pyaar Every Time", she talks about how every time we fall in love, it feels as if it's the first time.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-45)

Her other works, such as "To Like? Or To Love?" differentiate between loving and liking and how liking is free of boundaries while love is limiting.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-46) Jha's first open letter "A Letter To Myself" is about what she wants to tell her 15-year-old self in the past and that we should never compromise under any circumstance.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-47) In this collaboration with ITC Vivel, Jha inspires women to uncondition, challenge stereotypes and go forth to fulfill their dreams with confidence and say out loud, "Ab Samjhauta Nahin". She also presented a poem "Cheesy Stupid Ishq", as a narrator a day before the Valentines Day in 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sriti_Jha#cite_note-48)
